samf-junior-2006-r1-03.title: Groups of 4 points
samf-junior-2006-r1-03.body:
$36$ points is $36\div4=9$ groups of $4$ points. Each group needs R75, so Sipho spent $9\times75=\text{R}675$.

**Answer: (E) R675**

samf-junior-2006-r1-05.title: Lowest common multiple
samf-junior-2006-r1-05.body:
$8=2^3$, $12=2^2\cdot3$, $30=2\cdot3\cdot5$, so the lcm is $2^3\cdot3\cdot5=120$. This is already a three-digit number, so the smallest such number is $120$.

**Answer: (B) 120**

samf-junior-2006-r1-07.title: Count girls and boys
samf-junior-2006-r1-07.body:
A girl has at least three sisters, so there are at least $4$ girls. A boy has at least three sisters (fine with $4$ girls) and at least one brother, so there are at least $2$ boys. A girl needs at least one brother, which $2$ boys provide. The minimum is $4+2=6$.

**Answer: (C) 6**

samf-junior-2006-r1-08.title: Count
samf-junior-2006-r1-08.body:
$4^2=16$ and $4^3=64$. The whole numbers strictly between are $17,18,\dots,63$, which is $63-17+1=47$ numbers.

**Answer: (C) 47**

samf-junior-2006-r1-09.title: Fraction of an hour
samf-junior-2006-r1-09.body:
The hand moves from the 4 to the 5 in one hour. $\frac25$ of an hour is $\frac25\times60=24$ minutes, so the time is $04{:}24$.

**Answer: (D) 04:24**

samf-junior-2006-r1-10.title: Count paths
samf-junior-2006-r1-10.body:
Every route has $3$ steps east and $2$ steps south in some order: $\binom52=10$ routes.

**Answer: (B) 10**

samf-junior-2006-r1-10.title: Add up the ways
samf-junior-2006-r1-10.body:
Write at each corner the number of routes to it: the top row and left column have $1$ each; every other corner is the sum of the one above and to the left. The grid is $1,1,1,1\,/\,1,2,3,4\,/\,1,3,6,10$, so the bottom-right corner has $10$.

**Answer: (B) 10**

samf-junior-2006-r1-12.title: Worst case
samf-junior-2006-r1-12.body:
In the worst case she draws two beads of each colour (six beads) without three of a kind. The seventh bead must give three of one colour. With only six beads she could still have two of each colour, so $7$ beads are needed.

**Answer: (C) 7**

samf-junior-2006-r1-13.title: Read the graph
samf-junior-2006-r1-13.body:
A straight line in a distance-time graph means equal distances in equal times. The speed (the gradient) is constant.

**Answer: (E) travelling at a constant speed**

samf-junior-2006-r1-14.title: Algebra
samf-junior-2006-r1-14.body:
Let the numbers be $x$ and $x+1$, so $p=x(x+1)=x^2+x$. Then $(x+1)^2-x=x^2+2x+1-x=x^2+x+1=p+1$.

**Answer: (D) $p+1$**

samf-junior-2006-r1-15.title: Subsets
samf-junior-2006-r1-15.body:
Each weight is either used or not: $2^4=16$ choices, minus the choice of using no weights at all, leaves $15$ combinations. They give every whole mass from $1$ kg to $15$ kg.

**Answer: (A) 15**

samf-junior-2006-r1-16.title: Inscribed angle
samf-junior-2006-r1-16.body:
The octagon is inscribed in a circle, and its vertices cut the circle into $8$ equal arcs of $45^\circ$. The angle $x$ is an inscribed angle that stands on the arc of $3$ sides ($135^\circ$), so $x=\frac12\cdot135^\circ=67\frac12^\circ$.

**Answer: (C) $67\frac12$**

samf-junior-2006-r1-16.title: Isosceles triangles
samf-junior-2006-r1-16.body:
Each interior angle of the octagon is $135^\circ$. At the top-right vertex $x$ sits between the two chords. The triangle formed by that vertex and the next two vertices is isosceles with apex $135^\circ$, so its base angle there is $22\frac12^\circ$. The quadrilateral with three octagon sides (ending at the chord) is an isosceles trapezoid with angles $135^\circ,135^\circ,45^\circ,45^\circ$, so the angle between the side and the long chord is $45^\circ$. Hence $x=135^\circ-45^\circ-22\frac12^\circ=67\frac12^\circ$.

**Answer: (C) $67\frac12$**

samf-junior-2006-r1-17.title: Telescoping
samf-junior-2006-r1-17.body:
$\frac1{k(k+1)}=\frac1k-\frac1{k+1}$. Start with $\frac1{1\times2}=\frac12$. Then $\frac1{2\times3}+\dots+\frac1{49\times50}=\frac12-\frac1{50}$. The value is $\frac12-\left(\frac12-\frac1{50}\right)=\frac1{50}$.

**Answer: (E) $\frac1{50}$**

samf-junior-2006-r1-17.title: Pattern
samf-junior-2006-r1-17.body:
$\frac12-\frac16=\frac13$, $\frac13-\frac1{12}=\frac14$, $\frac14-\frac1{20}=\frac15$, so after subtracting up to $\frac1{n(n+1)}$ the value is $\frac1{n+1}$. For $n=49$: $\frac1{50}$.

**Answer: (E) $\frac1{50}$**

samf-junior-2006-r1-18.title: Triangular numbers
samf-junior-2006-r1-18.body:
Row $n$ has $n$ numbers, and the last number of row $n$ is $\frac{n(n+1)}2$. Row $50$ ends with $\frac{50\cdot51}2=1275$, so row $51$ runs from $1276$ to $1326$ ($51$ numbers). The middle (26th) number is $1275+26=1301$.

**Answer: (B) 1301**

samf-junior-2006-r1-19.title: Triangle conditions
samf-junior-2006-r1-19.body:
Let the parallelogram have sides of $a$ and $b$ matchsticks and the longer diagonal $c$ matchsticks. Then $2a+2b+c=42$, so $c$ is even and $a+b=21-\frac c2$. The diagonal and two sides form a triangle, so $c<a+b$. Since the diagonal is the longer one, the angle opposite it is obtuse, so $c^2>a^2+b^2$.

- $c=14$: $a+b=14$, not greater than $c$. No.
- $c=12$: $a+b=15$ and $a^2+b^2<144$: $(a,b)=(7,8),(6,9),(5,10),(4,11)$ work ($113,117,125,137$); $(3,12)$ gives $153$, too big. 4 ways.
- $c=10$: $a+b=16$, but $a^2+b^2\ge128>100$. No.
- $c\le8$: $a^2+b^2$ is even larger compared with $c^2$. No.

There are $4$ ways.

**Answer: (A) 4**

samf-junior-2006-r1-20.title: Use the side
samf-junior-2006-r1-20.body:
Let the hexagon have side $s$. The shaded triangle has the bottom side as base ($s$) and its apex at the midpoint of the top side, so its height is the full height of the hexagon, $\sqrt3\,s$. Its area is $\frac{\sqrt3}2s^2$. The hexagon has area $6\cdot\frac{\sqrt3}4s^2=\frac{3\sqrt3}2s^2$. The ratio is $\frac13$.

**Answer: (D) $\frac13$**

samf-junior-2006-r1-20.title: Six equilateral triangles
samf-junior-2006-r1-20.body:
Split the hexagon into $6$ equilateral triangles from its centre, each of area $t$. The bottom triangle has the bottom side as base and height $h_0$ (from the centre). The shaded triangle has the same base but its apex is on the top side, which is at distance $2h_0$ from the bottom side. So its area is $2t$ and the fraction is $\frac{2t}{6t}=\frac13$.

**Answer: (D) $\frac13$**
